summary: A billfish with a towering sail-shaped dorsal fin and a slender bill. It feeds on schooling fish and squid and is a major sport-fishing attraction off Kuala Rompin, Pahang.
nativeRange: Tropical and subtropical oceans; this profile focuses on Indo-Pacific populations.

features: Very tall sail-shaped first dorsal fin
Vertical bands made of blue spots on the sides

habitat.description: Upper ocean waters, also approaching continental coasts, islands and reefs.
habitat.diet: Schooling fish, squid and other small animal prey.

malaysia.rules: Many Rompin charter operators practise catch-and-release for billfish. This is an operator practice, not a claim of a nationwide legal requirement; confirm the applicable rules with the Department of Fisheries.

fishing.season: Rompin operators commonly fish March–October, with some extending into early November; quoted season dates vary. August–October is commonly reported as the peak. The November–February northeast monsoon can bring rough seas and suspend trips.
